coverage.assessment: Three setups are thinned. The college's formal requirement behind 'frankly tell the boys' is cut. The first draft dropped the step from 'Pteraspis grins' to choosing law as subject. The revision drops the King achievements that ground 'richest'. Also unexplained: 'full tide of fashion' (the Versailles crowning was cut). The Review-to-King setup does precede King, as planned.

The rooms, the route from Laramie to Long's Peak, the cabin and the shared bed are all clear. The mule now first appears as 'his mule' at the moment of cinching. 'Sioux' arrives without the Indians/troopers context. Both are minor.
The only performed speech, the Chicago answer, is kept verbatim. It is correctly framed as one student's reply to Adams's question.

Adams's hedged concession after the Chicago answer ('So far as it went, the answer was good') is cut. So is the colleagues' 'perhaps be frauds' hedge. The tone tilts toward flat dismay. The seven-year and 1877 anticipations are framed as planned.
The conditional prediction is kept with no hint of King's later failure. The elderly narrator's ironic distance is maintained. Nothing anticipates the later silence.

Signature images are lost from the King portrait: the triadic 'even women' gag, the Alcibiades comparison and the catalogue of energies. The students' 'burst open like flowers' image is also gone. Aphorisms survive, but the connective irony around them is thinner.

King as the 'model' loses its rationale, because the 'better system' and the 'education all of a piece' are both cut. The parallelism aphorism is stated without the west/east convergence that applies it to the two men.
All three dependencies hold in both the local text and the partner revisions (017, 023).

dependencies.assessment: The local V6 is kept. The partner 017 revision retains the Wenlock Edge introduction of Pteraspis and Siluria.

evidence.quote: they were shaped with the Pteraspis in Siluria
the ganoid fish, whose name, according to Professor Huxley, was Pteraspis

dependencies.assessment: The prediction is kept verbatim with no hint of failure. The 023 revision retains King's ambitious course and the doubt about its outcome.

evidence.quote: With ordinary luck he would die at eighty the richest and most many-sided genius of his day.
King had followed the ambitious course.

dependencies.assessment: The Lyell link survives locally, though the 'friends were sorely few' rationale is cut. The 017 revision retains Adams volunteering to review Lyell's Principles.

evidence.quote: Thanks to the article on Sir Charles Lyell, Adams passed for a friend of geologists.
young Adams offered to do it himself if Sir Charles would tell him what to say

findings.claim: The revision cuts the college's expectation that he teach elementary dates and the remark 'This was formal'. Without them, 'He could frankly tell the boys' now opens the paragraph with no context for the bargain. The revision also cuts the difficulty of getting students to talk at all.
findings.counterevidence: The bargain remains intelligible on its own terms.

evidence.quote: This was formal; and he could frankly tell the boys that, provided they passed their examinations
The college expected him to pass at least half his time teaching the boys a few elementary dates and relations
He could frankly tell the boys that, provided they passed their examinations, they might get their facts where they liked

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's sentence 'The college expected him...' followed by 'This was formal; and'.
findings.plan_relation: required (essential: students may get facts where they like)
findings.reader_effect: Adams's frank deal reads as arbitrary laxity rather than a dry response to an imposed formality. The argument for 'talk' as the only privilege loses its counterweight.
findings.title: The 'facts where they liked' bargain loses the college requirement it answers

findings.claim: The first draft cut 'One may not begin at the beginning' and the sentence about forcing his material into a shape for a method. The text therefore leaps from the Pteraspis image to 'He could think only of law as subject'. The irony of 'The course began with the beginning' is lost. The revision also cuts the hare-chasing gain and 'could not make it actual', which both qualified 'triumphant'.
findings.counterevidence: 'Merely antiquarian' still supplies the essential verdict.

evidence.quote: Adams found himself obliged to force his material into some shape to which a method could be applied.
The Pteraspis grins horribly from the closed entrance. He could think only of law as subject; the Law School as end
The Pteraspis grins horribly from the closed entrance. He could think only of law as subject; the Law School as end

findings.minimal_repair: Restore 'One may not begin at the beginning... Adams found himself obliged to force his material into some shape to which a method could be applied.'
findings.plan_relation: required (essential: method, triumphant but leading nowhere)
findings.reader_effect: The choice of law looks unmotivated. The double verdict, a real pedagogical gain that nonetheless led nowhere, is flattened.
findings.title: Step from 'Pteraspis grins' to choosing law is missing

findings.claim: The revision cuts the image of the students' minds bursting open 'like flowers', which the first draft kept. It also cuts 'So far as it went, the answer was good, and settled one's doubts', so the Chicago answer goes straight to Adams's self-doubt. The colleagues' 'perhaps be frauds' hedge is likewise removed.
findings.counterevidence: 'Excellent company' and the pathos of their faith survive.

evidence.quote: So far as it went, the answer was good, and settled one's doubts.
Cast more or less in the same mould, without violent emotions or sentiment, their minds burst open like flowers
for the degree of Harvard College had been rather a drawback to a young man in Boston and Washington. He still had to take for granted

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the 'burst open like flowers' clause and the 'So far as it went...' sentence.
findings.plan_relation: required (essential: students as only success; Chicago answer)
findings.reader_effect: This weakens why the students were the 'only success'. It also loses Adams's characteristic ironic acceptance of the market answer.
findings.title: Students' 'flowers' image and Adams's hedged concession cut

findings.claim: The first draft dropped King's 'education all of a piece, yet broad'. The revision further cuts Adams's claim that he would begin again 'on a better system'. The chapter thus no longer states what King is a model of, which is a coherent education set against Adams's accidental one.
findings.counterevidence: 'logically, scientifically' and the 'straight line' still imply the contrast.

evidence.quote: if he were to begin again, he would do it on a better system. He thought he knew nearly what system to pursue.
but he held that it was wrong, and that, if he were to begin again, he would do it on a better system.
With this result Henry Adams's education, at his entry into life, stopped, and his life began. The editorship
He had given himself education all of a piece, yet broad.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'but he held that it was wrong... better system' clause, and/or the 'all of a piece' sentence.
findings.plan_relation: planning omission partly; required setup under 'model' essential
findings.reader_effect: This weakens the chapter's argumentative arc from failed education to a personified ideal. It also blunts the contrast in 'violent breaks or waves'.
findings.title: King as 'model' loses the 'better system' premise

findings.claim: The first draft replaced the companion-charm paragraph with the phrase 'than charm'. The revision then cuts the 'even women' triad, the wit/energy/generosity catalogue and the Alcibiades comparison. The only remaining 'charm' is King's seeing more than others, so the contrast in 'far more vital than charm' points at the wrong quality.
findings.counterevidence: The optional women's-jealousy paragraph was legitimately cut.

evidence.quote: As a companion, King's charm was great, but this was not the quality that so much attracted Adams
He had in him something of the Greek--a touch of Alcibiades or Alexander.
the charm of King was that he saw what others did and a great deal more. One Clarence King only existed in the world.
King and the Fortieth Parallel influenced him in a way far more vital than charm.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'His wit and humor...Nature herself' sentence and the Greek sentence. Alternatively, change 'than charm' to 'than charm of company'.
findings.reader_effect: The essential 'King's qualities' are reduced to knowledge lists. 'One Clarence King only existed' is less earned, and a key comic triad in the author's voice is gone.
findings.title: King portrait stripped; 'far more vital than charm' lacks its anchor

findings.claim: The revision ends the paragraph on the general requirement of 'parallelism of life'. It cuts the image of King coming 'from the west' and Adams 'from the east' with the same problems, implements and obstacles, which the first draft kept.
findings.counterevidence: 'The lines of their lives converged' partly carries the idea.

evidence.quote: The one, coming from the west, saturated with the sunshine of the Sierras, met the other, drifting from the east, drenched in the fogs of London
The one, coming from the west, saturated with the sunshine of the Sierras, met the other, drifting from the east
Friendship needs a certain parallelism of life, a community of thought, a rivalry of aim.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'The one, coming from the west... the same obstacles to overcome.'
findings.reader_effect: The aphorism floats free of the two men. The vivid Sierras/London antithesis that dramatizes the friendship is lost.
findings.title: Parallelism aphorism left unapplied; west/east convergence cut

findings.claim: The first draft cut the mining-fortune sentence. The revision also cuts the civil Government Survey and 'paralleled the Continental Railway in Geology'. 'Great success' is now backed only by a work in progress, and nothing prepares the 'richest' of the kept prediction.
findings.counterevidence: The 'Whatever prize he wanted' sentence survives, and so does the prediction itself.

evidence.quote: take the pick of the gold and silver, copper or coal, and build up his fortune as he pleased
He had organized, as a civil--not military--measure, a Government Survey. He had paralleled the Continental Railway in Geology.
King's abnormal energy had already won him great success. He was creating one of the classic scientific works of the century.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the two Survey/Railway sentences and the short 'take the pick of the gold and silver...' clause.
findings.reader_effect: The planned contrast of achievements with Adams's broken life weakens. The prediction's financial half reads as unmotivated.
findings.title: King's achievements thinned; 'richest' unprepared

findings.claim: The revision cuts 'he liked to wander off alone on his mule'. The mule now first appears as 'his mule' while being cinched, and why Adams is alone goes unexplained.
findings.counterevidence: The sense remains clear from context.

evidence.quote: he liked to wander off alone on his mule, and pass the day fishing a mountain stream or exploring a valley
Adams liked to wander off alone on his mule
until at last when the fisherman cinched his mule, sunset was nearer than he thought

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's one-sentence habit line.
findings.reader_effect: This is a small bump before the mule becomes the agent that finds the cabin.
findings.title: Mule and solitary-wandering habit introduced late

strengths: The Everett drawing-room memory is paired cleanly with Adams renting the same room, with Brooks above and Dennett opposite.
The Estes Park sequence keeps its comic timing intact: the sun and fish line, the 'allowed' he was lost, the mule cleverer than himself, the shared bed and talk till dawn.
The parent/murderer/teacher triad and the 'incoherent and immoral' dilemma are preserved in their exact argumentative order.
The Harvard ironies are kept whole: Eliot's hint, 'redeemed America', 'Ignorance paid better', and the closing 'submissive' punchline.
summary: The revision keeps every planned verbatim passage, essential beat and continuity check. That includes the anticipatory framing of the seven years and 1877, Brooks as a law student, Emmons as a Quincy neighbor, Greeley and the buggy, and age thirty-three. The prediction about King also survives intact. No finding blocks publication. The revision's extra compression, however, thins several connective hinges. These include the college's formal requirement behind the 'facts where they liked' bargain, the 'better system' that makes King a model, and King's qualities and achievements, so that 'than charm' and 'richest' land weakly. It also cuts the west/east convergence that applies the friendship aphorism to King and Adams. A few small source restorations would fix most of these.
